Can the bank demand payment from me as a guarantor before taking legal action against the main borrower?

No, the bank is not required to exhaust its rights or take action against the borrower or any other guarantor before requiring you to make a payment under the agreement. (south_indian_bank_loan.pdf, p.4)

Who is responsible for paying the various costs, taxes, and legal expenses associated with my loan agreement?

The Borrower is solely responsible for bearing and paying all present and future costs, expenses, taxes, levies, and stamp duties related to the loan documents or transactions, including expenses incurred by the Bank for the creation, enforcement, or preservation of security and any legal proceedings. If the Bank pays these amounts, the Borrower must reimburse the Bank in full or authorize the Bank to debit their account. (south_indian_bank_loan.pdf, p.3)

What is the extent of a guarantor's responsibility if the borrower fails to meet their loan obligations?

The guarantor is jointly and severally liable to irrevocably and unconditionally guarantee the full performance of the loan agreement and collateral documents. If the borrower fails to perform any part of these agreements, the guarantor must pay the bank the sums due upon demand. (south_indian_bank_loan.pdf, p.4)

How long do I have to dispute the terms of my loan agreement after I have signed and received it?
You must provide written notification to the Bank regarding any discrepancies in the Loan Agreement within 7 days after signing and delivery of the document. (standard_chartered_loan.pdf, p.2)

Can the bank change the terms or fees of my loan without giving me any prior notice?

Generally, the bank will provide at least 30 days' notice for changes to fees and charges. However, they are not required to give advance notice if the changes are due to an emergency, if providing notice is not practicable, if the amendments are administrative or clarificatory in nature, or if they are adding terms for new products or services. (cimb_personal_loan.pdf, p.3)

Can CIBC use money they owe me to pay off my loan balance if I am in financial trouble?

Yes. CIBC may, without notice, set off or compensate any obligation they owe you against any amount you owe them under your loan agreement. This right can be exercised immediately if they receive notice of your bankruptcy, insolvency, or a similar arrangement. (cibc_personal_loan.pdf, p.9)

Am I responsible for paying taxes on my loan payments to the bank?

Yes, you are responsible for all goods and services taxes or other levies related to your loan. If any tax deduction is required from your payment, you must pay an additional amount to ensure the bank receives the full sum it would have otherwise received (cimb_personal_loan.pdf, p.3).
